scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. prediction.raw: I would rate this scenario as: 1 (YTA - You're The Asshole) I think it was wrong to delete your stepbrother's profile without considering his feelings or the effort he put into his Zelda save. While it's understandable that you wanted to simplify your Switch experience, deleting his profile without warning or discussing it with him was thoughtless and inconsiderate. As a responsible and caring sibling, you should have considered the potential impact on your stepbrother before taking such an action. You had created a profile for him and allowed him to play on your Switch, which implies that you were willing to share your device with him. By deleting his profile, you not only erased his progress but also disregarded his emotional investment in the game. It's not just about the practical aspect of having to click on your profile each time; it's about being respectful and considerate of others' feelings and property. Your stepbrother was enjoying playing on your Switch, and you should have found an alternative solution, such as creating a separate account or discussing with him how to manage the device, rather than simply deleting his profile. Your dad's reaction and your stepbrother's emotional response suggest that your actions were indeed hurtful and inconsiderate. It's essential to be more empathetic and communicative in the future, especially when it comes to shared devices and personal belongings.
